html:
The Waitangi Tribunal is a permanent New Zealand body, set up in 1975, that hears claims by Māori that the Crown broke the promises of the Treaty of Waitangi of 1840.

It was created by the Treaty of Waitangi Act, pushed through by the Labour minister of Māori affairs Matiu Rata. The same year a land march led by Whina Cooper walked the length of the North Island to protest the loss of Māori land.

At first the tribunal could only look at events after 1975. In 1985 its reach was extended back to 1840, and claims about land taken in the New Zealand Wars and by later purchases flooded in.

The tribunal is not a court and most of its findings are only advice. But its long reports rewrote New Zealand's history and laid the ground for settlements in which the government apologised and returned land and money to iwi (tribes), starting with Waikato-Tainui in 1995 and Ngāi Tahu in 1998.
sum: The Waitangi Tribunal is a permanent New Zealand body, set up in 1975, that hears claims by Māori that the Crown broke the promises of the Treaty of Waitangi of 1840.
